Deployment and upgrade preferences clarified by Jordi on 2026-09-06 for Zenod: this is currently a single-user live service. For this release, deploy reviewed incremental changes to the existing production environment, test through the direct Zenod MCP connection, and fix bounded problems. Make undo easy: retain previous immutable image and exact configuration, preserve data volumes/sessions, and have a ready rollback command. Keep the change small; remove complexity only when convenient within the work, otherwise defer it. Maintain a durable deployments/upgrades spine leaf so the supported upgrade procedure and learnings are reused instead of reinvented. Do not introduce a new staging/provider setup as a prerequisite when the authorized live environment is available. Scope future permissions to the user's actual request; this does not authorize unrelated future deployments, billing or public signup. Engineering learnings: MCP success did not prove customer chat behavior; use shared read/coverage/grounding finalization and test streaming plus persisted history. Verify actual running container image and source revision, not merely desired configuration. Distinguish code rollback from data restore. Full backup/off-host restore proofs are expensive; define a risk-based recurring backup policy rather than repeating ad hoc ceremony.
